solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Comic news bulletin from Spooner at Little Bighorn?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the headline's two words trade their first sounds

parts.note: General George Custer was the commander at the Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876
the headline from that battle was that Custer was beaten

explanation.surface: A reporter files a headline from the 1876 battlefield, delivered in the muddled style of Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: The news from Little Bighorn is CUSTER BEATEN; swapping the opening sounds gives the silent-film comedian, with the second word spelt KEATON.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was a celebrated comedian of American silent cinema, so he is a comic.

clue.text: Dollar bill avoided by Donald Trump?

parts.note: the dollar is the currency of the US, as in US dollar
a draft is a bill of exchange, an order for payment

explanation.surface: A dollar note that a famous president supposedly dodged.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Trump received deferments and never served during the Vietnam-era call-up, hence the question mark on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The American military call-up of the 1960s is something Trump famously escaped through deferments.

clue.text: Convert to eg holy study of religion

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn something holy into a course of religious study, with a convert in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Theology is the academic discipline concerned with God and religious belief.

clue.text: Healthy-looking Rovers striker embracing son

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the striker's name holds the letter for son

parts.note: Roy Race is the centre forward of Melchester Rovers in the British comic strip Roy of the Rovers

explanation.surface: A fit-looking footballer from Rovers hugging his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy of the Rovers is a long-running British football comic strip, so its striker is ROY.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosy complexion, pink-cheeked, suggests good health.

clue.text: Witness former VP suppressing rising anger

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-husband

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down within, so the vice-president's name holds the angry word

parts.note: Mike Pence was US vice-president under Trump

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A one-time American vice-president keeping a lid on mounting fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witness' looks like a noun for an onlooker, but here it is the verb meaning to live through.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to undergo or live through it, a verb sense shared with experience.

clue.text: Time to do something about independence, it's understood

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the action word wraps the letter for independence

parts.note: to act is to do something
I is an abbreviation for independence, also for independent

explanation.surface: A call for action over a nation's independence, with the assumption that everyone already knows.
explanation.walkthrough: ACT goes around I to give ACIT, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied without being stated, so it is understood rather than spoken.

clue.text: Terrible rain over outskirts of Burundi capital

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of the weather word are jumbled

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the outskirts are the outer edges, so only the first and last letters of the country are used

explanation.surface: Awful weather sweeping across the fringes of an African country's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges RAIN to NAIR; 'outskirts of' Burundi gives BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, in East Africa near Burundi.

clue.text: Hollywood giant's Byzantine bulky artefact?

definitions.note: the definition reads as 'Hollywood giant is', the clue's possessive acting as a verb

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A large Hollywood figure described as an elaborate, bulky museum piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Roscoe Arbuckle, a big silent-film comedian, was himself a bulky figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Roscoe Arbuckle was a large silent-era comedy star, a giant of early Hollywood in both senses.

clue.text: Head of science institute loaned old Scot original English work featuring 1, 8 or the 28?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lent means loaned
the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland
ur- is a prefix meaning original, as in Urtext

explanation.surface: A chain of scholarly events: a science chief, an institute, a loan to an ancient Scot, an English original.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references point to the comedian at 1, the star at 8 and the bumbling police at 28, all silent-era screen names.
explanation.definitionFit: A film made without synchronised sound is a silent picture, the medium in which those comedians made their names.

clue.text: He's taken off ceremonial hat to deliver speech

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so those letters come out of the hat word

parts.note: a headdress is an ornamental head covering worn on ceremonial occasions
read as 'he is', supplying the letters HE that are removed

explanation.surface: A dignitary removes his ceremonial headgear before giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk delivered to an audience, so it is a speech.

clue.text: Italian barman returning home with endless hiccups

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: without its ends, so the first and last letters of the word are dropped

explanation.surface: An Italian bartender comes back to the house still suffering from hiccups that won't stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims HICCUPS to ICCUP; IN plus ICCUP, 'returning', becomes PUCCINI. A composer writes in musical bars, hence a 'barman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini was an Italian opera composer, and composers write music divided into bars.

clue.text: Go fishing, bitterly cold in Tobol on vacation

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the cold word sits within the remaining letters of the river
vacated means emptied, so the inner letters of the river's name are removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: raw weather is bitterly cold

explanation.surface: Going fishing in freezing weather on the Tobol, a Siberian river, while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To trawl is to fish by dragging a large net behind a boat.

clue.text: 16 at sea — a few tending to worry

parts.note: 16 across is a light fog; a fret is a sea fog rolling in from the coast, as in sea fret
some means a few

explanation.surface: Fog rolling in at sea, and a few people anxious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea fret is a coastal fog in northern England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretsome describes a person inclined to fret, that is, given to anxiety.

clue.text: Top actor Rhames under pressure, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade their first sounds

parts.note: Ving Rhames is an American actor, known for Pulp Fiction
stressed means under pressure

explanation.surface: A leading actor feeling the strain, in a Spooner-style muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of VING and STRESSED gives the sound of the mesh undergarment; a string vest is a British-style open-weave vest.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is a garment worn on the upper body, which is a top.

clue.text: Totally special to get Hermes trousers

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the words keep the answer tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A special deal to obtain designer Hermes trousers, from the Parisian fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is an adverb meaning completely or in total, matching totally.

clue.text: Monsieur's first film?

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, French for Mr
first is written 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's debut motion picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests a movie but means a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A film of condensation or vapour is a thin coating, like a haze on glass.

clue.text: C'mon men! I ordered a reminder!

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: An exasperated boss demanding the team follow up on a reminder he ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A mnemonic is a memory aid, a rhyme or device that prompts recall.

clue.text: Republican leaves loud party

indicators.note: when someone leaves they depart, so that letter goes from the word for loud

parts.note: brash means loud and showy

explanation.surface: A Republican walks out of a noisy party.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is informal for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Scots departed to visit part of Guernsey, an island state

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so the Scots word goes inside the island

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands within the Bailiwick of Guernsey
awa is Scots for away, meaning gone

explanation.surface: Scots leaving to tour part of the Channel Islands, on their way to an island state.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarawak is a Malaysian state on the island of Borneo.

clue.text: Send over Britannic nickel to insulate home for some Ohioans?

indicators.note: to send over is to turn something over, so the concealed letters are read backwards
insulating means wrapping up, so the words wrap the answer inside them

explanation.surface: An instruction to ship British nickel to insulate a house for people in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Britannic' and 'nickel' look like separate pieces, but together they hold ITANNICNIC, which 'Send over' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cincinnati is a large city in the state of Ohio, where many Ohioans live.

clue.text: Song's cool … is it one by Zeppelin?

parts.note: an air is a song or tune, and the possessive supplies the S
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A cool song: is it one by Led Zeppelin?
explanation.walkthrough: Zeppelin looks like the rock band, but it is Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin, maker of dirigibles.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Zeppelin built rigid dirigible balloons, so a craft of his is a lighter-than-air vessel.

clue.text: Phoenician state wagon — Tyre's last — transporting crone

indicators.note: to transport is to carry, so the vehicle and the letter carry the old woman inside

parts.note: a cart is a wagon

indicators.note: the possessive 'Tyre's last' points to the final letter of the port's name

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman, a crone

explanation.surface: A cart from Tyre, the Phoenician port, carrying an old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was a city-state founded by Phoenician colonists from Tyre in North Africa.

clue.text: Scary, like Esau

definitions.meaning: informally, a frightening or dangerous situation
in Genesis, Esau was described as a ... man, unlike his smooth brother Jacob

explanation.surface: Biblical Esau described as frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is British slang for frightening, and it also means covered in thick body hair, as Esau was.

clue.text: Middle East artist regularly getting distinction

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern painter routinely winning honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the second, fourth and sixth letters of artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is excellence deserving praise, a distinction such as an award grade.

clue.text: Unlock old enclosure

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Releasing the gate of an old animal pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlock a door is to unfasten it so it can be swung wide.

clue.text: Folding towel, I'd time for a walk on the beach?

definitions.text: time for a walk on the beach?

indicators.note: folding something changes its shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone folding up a towel, deciding it's the moment for a seaside stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: When the sea is furthest out, wide stretches of sand are exposed for strolling.

clue.text: Knight blocking way in front of Her Majesty is just a big pussycat

indicators.note: the first part is placed ahead of the royal letters
something blocking a route stands inside it, so the chess letter sits in the way

parts.note: a path is a way
N is the chess notation for knight
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A knight standing in the Queen's way turns out to be a harmless softie.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside PATH to give PANTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A leopard, especially a black one, is a large wild cat, playfully a big pussycat.

clue.text: Corrupt tycoons keep special constables in action

indicators.note: something corrupted is spoilt and altered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Crooked business magnates retain part-time police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special constables' reads as one British phrase for volunteer police, but 'special' is split off as S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Keystone Cops were bumbling silent-film policemen whose slapstick chases were all action.
